question: How does Caddy replace a running configuration without discarding the old one before the new applications are ready, and where can the handoff fail?

observations.text: changeConfig locks rawCfgMu and defers its unlock.
The requested mutation is applied to rawCfg, then the complete resulting configuration is marshaled into newCfg.
When forceReload is false and newCfg equals rawCfgJSON, changeConfig returns errSameConfig before loading.
Configuration object IDs are indexed before loading; an indexing error restores the prior raw configuration representation when one exists.
changeConfig calls unsyncedDecodeAndRun with newCfg; when it returns an error, changeConfig restores the prior raw configuration representation and returns an error.
rawCfgJSON and rawCfgIndex are assigned the new values only after unsyncedDecodeAndRun succeeds.
unsyncedDecodeAndRun removes meta fields and strictly unmarshals the result into a new Config.
unsyncedDecodeAndRun calls run(newCfg, true) and returns immediately if run fails.
After run succeeds, unsyncedDecodeAndRun saves currentCtx as oldCtx, assigns the new context while holding currentCtxMu, unlocks, and then calls unsyncedStop(oldCtx).
run provisions the new context first; a provisioning error is returned before application startup.
With startup enabled, run starts applications from ctx.cfg.apps; if one start fails, it stops the applications already recorded as started and returns an error.
After application startup, run emits the started event, calls finishSettingUp, and returns the resulting error.
During provisioning, replaceAdminServer is called before configured applications are loaded and provisioned.
unsyncedStop emits stopping, calls Stop for every application while continuing after logged errors, and then invokes the configuration context cancel function.
